statement:
For each positive integer \(n\) consider the sequence of 2004 integers
\[\lfloor n + \sqrt{n} \rfloor,\; \lfloor n+1 + \sqrt{n+1} \rfloor,\; \lfloor n+2 + \sqrt{n+2} \rfloor,\; \ldots,\; \lfloor n+2003 + \sqrt{n+2003} \rfloor.\]
Determine the smallest integer \(n\) such that these 2004 numbers are 2004 consecutive integers.

Determine all positive integers \(a, b, c, d\) such that
\[a < b, \quad a^2 c = b^2 d, \quad ab + cd = 2^{99} + 2^{101}.\]

Zeros and ones are placed in each cell of a rectangular board. The board is called varied if each row contains at least one 0 and at least two 1s. Given \(n \geq 3\), find all integers \(k > 1\) with the following property: the columns of every varied board of \(k\) rows and \(n\) columns can be permuted so that in each row the 1s do not form a consecutive block (i.e., there are at least two 1s separated by one or more 0s).

Determine all positive integers \(a\) and \(b\) such that each cell of an \(a \times b\) board can be colored red, blue, or green so that every red cell has exactly one blue neighbor and one green neighbor, every blue cell has exactly one red and one green neighbor, and every green cell has exactly one red and one blue neighbor. (Two cells are neighbors if they share a side.)
The pentagon \(ABCDE\) has \(AB = BC\), \(CD = DE\), \(\angle ABC = 120^\circ\), \(\angle CDE = 60^\circ\), and \(BD = 2\). Calculate the area of the pentagon.

Decide if it is possible to generate an infinite sequence of positive integers \(a_n\) such that no three terms form an arithmetic progression and for all \(n\),
\[|a_n - n^2| < \frac{n}{2}.\]
Clarification: Three numbers \(a, b, c\) are in arithmetic progression if and only if \(2b = a + c\).
